search_log: Searched "Stephen King The Dead Zone excerpt first chapter publisher", "The Dead Zone Stephen King point of view third person narrator", "The Dead Zone Stephen King Google Books excerpt", and "The Dead Zone novel third-person narration scholarly analysis".

Opened StephenKing.com, Simon & Schuster, Google Books, and Hodder/Hachette title pages. They verified the work and editions, but their synopses were not narrator-person evidence; Hodder's Read Excerpt control did not expose additional prose.
Searched Open Library and Internet Archive availability. Open Library exposed only the third-person opening sentence for the English edition, so it was retained as limited Tier D evidence.
Opened the Cambridge scholarly chapter and found an explicit whole-novel description of a third-person omniscient narrator.
Searched "The Dead Zone third person omniscient" and opened the BookRags style discussion as an additional explicit whole-book description.

Opened and searched a complete Scribner eBook text for the sampled quotations and for opening, interior, and ending structure. This resolved clipped I/we/you passages as dialogue, hypothetical thought, a letter, or testimony rather than alternating base narration.
person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and third person, with omniscient or shifting limited access to Sarah, Johnny, Stillson, and other characters. Multiple quote passages independently expose that position through sustained external narration and access to characters' thoughts. Live full-text checks resolved the potentially contrary I, we, and you quotations as dialogue, generic maxims, Johnny's hypothetical Question, or other local material; the ending's first-person letter and testimony are explicitly embedded documents rather than autonomous first-person narrative sections. The quote evidence agrees with the Cambridge whole-book structural analysis and additional corroboration. The main limitation is that the complete searchable text was hosted by a third party, but the scholarly Tier B source and independent Goodreads-derived passages support the same classification with no credible conflict.
